CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic medical conditions

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male with past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension who presents for follow-up of his chronic problems. Patient reports having had a challenging year and a half, with anxiety and stress related to preparing for and hosting Thanksgiving gatherings after not seeing family for about two years. He states the holiday was good but involved considerable work and stress. He is planning to take a vacation to somewhere warm for the new year. Regarding depression, he has tried a new strategy over the summer of taking long walks outside every morning, which he enjoyed due to pleasant weather and blooming plants, and this encouraged him to do yard work on weekends as well. However, with seasonal changes and cold weather, he has been unable to continue this activity and needs to find new strategies. He is not ready to try medications at this time and would like to explore alternative options including therapy. He denies any suicidal or homicidal ideation. Regarding diabetes, he managed his sugar intake reasonably well through Halloween but did not adhere strictly to his diet during Thanksgiving week. He reports trying to monitor his diet more carefully since then and continues metformin. Regarding hypertension, he purchased a home blood pressure cuff as recommended and reports readings have been moderate with nothing out of the ordinary. He continues lisinopril without problems. He completed review of systems at check-in.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Depression
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
3. Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
1. Metformin
2. Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys outdoor activities including walking and yard work. Recently participated in holiday family gatherings.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well-controlled.
Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated.
Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at left base, consistent with prior examination.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities.

RESULTS
EKG: No concerning findings. No acute changes noted.
Hemoglobin A1C: 8.0 (elevated; goal less than 6.0)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Referred to psychiatry for talk therapy and counseling. Patient prefers non-medication approach at this time.
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1C in next couple of months. Order lipid panel.
3. Hypertension: Order echocardiogram to recheck systolic ejection murmur. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily.
